title: Stop Dumping on the Great Barrier Reef Bill 2014
short_title: Stop Dumping on the Great Barrier Reef Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit dumping dredged material in the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area and loading it for that purpose, subject to an earlier-approval exception.
It would create offences carrying up to 250 penalty units, 12 months' imprisonment or both, and prevent permits authorising the prohibited dumping or loading.
Activities approved on or before 9 December 2013 would be excluded, while later approvals, including Abbot Point's 10 December 2013 approval, would be affected.
changes: Existing permits for prohibited activities would cease to operate, subject to the earlier-approval exception.
States could not exempt the reef area from the new restrictions by declaration.
Strict liability would apply to the reef-location element of the dumping offence.
The legislation would commence on the day after royal assent.
summary.affected: Dredging operators, vessel and platform operators, permit holders and Commonwealth and state environmental administrators are affected.
